Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer

daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience designing and operating Java and Spring Boot services for insurance and travel products. Experience includes REST API design, relational databases, Kafka event streams, automated testing, CI/CD and cloud deployment. Improved API performance and reliability and participates in a production on-call rota.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and frameworks: Java 8–17, Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic), PHP
APIs and messaging: REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Databases and caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis
Cloud and deployment: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Jan 2022–Present
- Develop and maintain seven Java 17 and Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed a REST API for a partner quoting integration used by 12 broker partners, with versioning documented in OpenAPI.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, eliminating duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query improvements.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in on-call one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A. | Sep 2019–Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 and Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests using Testcontainers, increasing payment module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Helped split the monolith by extracting a notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer, internship then full-time | CodeFarol Lda | Jul 2018–Aug 2019
- Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018

LANGUAGES
English: fluent | Portuguese: fluent | Spanish: conversational

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is concise, professional, and well structured. It presents a strong progression from junior developer to backend engineer and uses quantified outcomes effectively, including the 75% reduction in p99 latency, 12 broker partners, seven microservices, and improved test coverage. The experience bullets are specific and technically credible. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role fit: the CV presents a strong Java backend profile while the target role is primarily Python-focused. It also does not explicitly demonstrate schema migrations or technical trade-off communication.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard bullets, searchable technology names, and reverse-chronological experience. It includes strong matches such as Java, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, automated testing, Jenkins, CI/CD, and on-call. AI screening probability is moderate to high for a general backend role, but lower for a strict Python-specific screen because Python and FastAPI are absent. The CV could improve keyword precision by using the exact phrase “query tuning” and by listing “CI/CD” explicitly in the technical skills section, both of which are supported by the existing content.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong comparable-language match through seven years of Java backend development and covers most of the platform engineering fundamentals: REST APIs, relational databases, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, automated testing, CI/CD, Kafka, Kubernetes, and production on-call. It aligns well with the company’s ownership and reliability culture through service operation, performance improvements, idempotent consumers, an outbox table, and on-call participation. The candidate's material does not show professional Python experience or stated willingness to work mainly in Python; this is a genuine role-fit gap rather than a CV-writing defect. Schema migrations, infrastructure as code/Terraform, observability tooling, logistics or EDI, and Dutch/French are also not supported by the candidate information. The CV does not currently evidence explaining technical trade-offs clearly, although the candidate's material does not provide a specific example for that requirement.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section under “Cloud and deployment,” change “AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins” to “AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins, CI/CD.” This makes the job-description keyword explicit and is supported by the existing Jenkins pipeline experience.
2. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, change “Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query improvements” to “Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query tuning, including fixing N+1 queries.” This uses the job ad’s exact “query tuning” terminology while remaining faithful to the original candidate information.
3. Do not add Python, FastAPI, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, logistics/EDI experience, schema migrations, or Dutch/French language skills to this CV unless the candidate can substantiate them; none are present in the Original Candidate Information.
